B: Hiya, how you doing? Craig. Can you hear me alright?
A: Yes, fine. Hi, I'm Nicola.
B: Nice one. Where you based, Nicola?
A: Basingstoke.
B: Lovely. I'm Cottingham, just outside Hull. How's your day going?
A: Fine. Busy. I'm a practice manager at a GP surgery, so it's always busy. What do you do?
B: Process operator at a chemical plant, out at Saltend. Twelve-hour shifts, days and nights. Just come off nights, so if I start talking rubbish, that's why.
A: Right. How do you sleep in the day?
B: Blackout blinds, earplugs, and the dog's banned from the bedroom. He's started barking at the postman again, so it's touch and go to be fair.
A: We've got a cat. She's quiet. She's just sick on the carpet instead.
B: Ha! Lovely. What's she called?
A: Biscuit. She's fifteen. She does what she wants.
B: That's cats, isn't it. So what's practice manager, is that like running the place?
A: Basically. Reception, admin staff, rotas, complaints, budgets, inspections. Monday mornings are carnage, to be honest. Phones open at eight and it's just a queue of angry people.
B: Oh, I bet. See, I'd be no good at that. If something goes wrong on plant I'm fine, I don't flap, but people shouting down a phone at me all day, I'd go mad. My wife Rachel's an accountant and it's her busy season, she's sat there till ten every night with spreadsheets, and I'm doing all the teas, which, believe me, is not a treat for anyone.
A: I do our household budget on a spreadsheet. Monthly.
B: You and Rachel'd get on. Saw your photo, the meal plan on the fridge. I thought, that's Rachel, that.
A: Well, somebody has to do it. My husband Darren would eat cereal for dinner otherwise.
B: Darren! I've just been talking to a Darren. Garden centre lad, Black Country. Great bloke.
A: Not mine, then. Mine's an electrician. Erm, sorry, did you get told what this is all for? Nobody's explained it to me.
B: Not a clue, to be honest. I just took it as a chat. Three minutes, have a natter, fill the form in.
A: Hm. I like to know what I'm being asked to do.
B: Fair enough. I'm the opposite, I just turn up. Do you get away much, holidays?
A: Tenerife. Same hotel, three times. And Cornwall.
B: Tenerife! Love it. We did Playa de las Americas, big group of us, absolute carnage. Brilliant.
A: That's not really what I go for. I go for the quiet. Sunbed, book, nobody needs anything from me.
B: No, that's fair, you've earned it with your Mondays. Sorry, I've gone off on one there. Do you
